text:
ellie: FYI ran into a rotation + cache mismatch in the CLI/sample app today. new team hit onboarding friction.

sam: details?

ellie: repro summary:
```bash
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-old
export REDWOOD_ORG=org-legacy
python examples/sample-app/worker.py &   # long-lived process caches creds
# infra rotates key -> sk-new for org-onboard
# worker keeps using sk-old until restart -> requests billed to org-legacy
```

jia: so in-memory client didn't refresh. which SDKs are affected?

ellie: python sample used a global client and had no auto-refresh. go and js samples vary: js has opt-in autoRefresh; go reads env once. inconsistent sample patterns are the root cause.

ops-bot: created ticket RW-5596 "worker-in-memory-key-rotation-mismatch" (prio: medium)

sam: short-term mitigations: document `redwood auth refresh`, add a SIGHUP sample to worker, and a `--watch-auth` CLI flag to reload on env changes.

docsy: I'll add a blurb to quickstart: "For long-lived processes enable SDK auto-refresh or call `redwood auth refresh` during deploys."

jia: long-term: standardize precedence (CLI flag > explicit param > env > session cache > system store), expose client.reload_credentials(), and add integration tests that rotate keys mid-run.

ellie: also found edge: REDWOOD_PROJECT set without REDWOOD_ORG can cause SDKs to infer org from stale session metadata and not rotate correctly. add a troubleshooting note.

sam: action items: 1) spike `--watch-auth` (1 day), 2) add sample SIGHUP handler to examples, 3) docs update, 4) telemetry events `auth.key_rotate_miss` + `auth.env_reload`. I'll own the spike.

ellie: attaching minimal reproducer to RW-5596 and will update sample-app readme. tagging @eng-devex @platform. thanks all :thumbsup:
